narrative.overview:
Every surface is a page of the shop's own appointment book: cool white ledger stock, graphite ink, pale blue ruling, and one rubber-stamp ink that belongs to the shop. Headings read like printed ledger headers, times and prices are set in tabular mono as if entered in the book, sections are reached through index tabs, closed time is hatched in graphite, and the one action is a stamp you press. Nothing is decorative that a real ledger would not carry.

The system is a template, not a brand. Its identity lives in the materials (paper, ink, ruling, stamp), never in trade imagery, so any appointment-based personal-care shop can wear it. A new shop changes words, numbers and exactly two colour inputs in `content/shop.ts` (`theme.stamp`, `theme.stampInk`); every other stamp shade is derived from them.

Density is that of a working document: strong horizontal rules, tight label type, generous display type, flat paper. Motion is ink being laid down, never floating: rules draw themselves in as they scroll into view, the OPEN / CLOSED stamp presses onto the week, the Book button compresses and twists slightly under the thumb, and the "now" line on the week grid moves in real time.
keyCharacteristics: Cool white ledger paper with pale blue ruling on a shared 2rem line.
One saturated colour: the shop's stamp ink, carried by a single token.
One type family (Archivo) stretched across its width axis for hierarchy; mono only for figures.
Near-square corners, hard ink rules, flat pages; the one lifted object is the appointment card.
Hatched graphite marks closed or unavailable time.
Motion grammar: ink draws, stamps press.

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: The stamp is the only saturated colour on the page, and it enters through one token. Components reference `stamp`, `stamp-deep`, `stamp-wash` or `stamp-ink`; they never hardcode a brand hex, and they never introduce a second accent.

rules.name: The Cool Paper Rule
rules.body: Paper is cool white with a blue-grey cast. It is never cream, beige or warm off-white.

rules.name: The Hatched Time Rule
rules.body: Closed or unavailable time is drawn with graphite hatching, not greyed out with opacity. Hatching means "the book is shut here" wherever it appears: week grid, duration cells, team day strips, placeholder frames.

rules.name: The Width Axis Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy comes from Archivo's width and weight, not from a second display family: 68% for ledger headings, 78% for labels, 92% for the lede, 100% for reading text. Do not add a serif or a script.

rules.name: The Figures-in-Mono Rule
rules.body: Any number a client reads to decide (time, price, duration, date) is set in the mono figure style. Prose never switches to mono except for these entries.

rules.name: The One Grout Rule
rules.body: Every ruled surface shares the 2rem ledger line (`--line`). Row heights on ruled surfaces (hero facts, mobile menu entries, card fields, week-grid hours) are multiples of it (1x, 1.5x, 2x), so ruling never drifts between components.

rules.name: The Flat Book Rule
rules.body: Pages, rows, tabs, grids and buttons never cast shadows. A shadow is reserved for an object that has left the book, and there is one.

dos: Do take every brand colour from `theme.stamp` and `theme.stampInk` and derive pressed and wash shades with `color-mix` in oklab.
Do draw structure with ink rules: 3px + 1px double rule over section heads, 1px ink for frames, 1px rule-strong inside lists and grids.
Do keep ruled surfaces on the 2rem `--line` and size ruled rows in whole or half multiples of it.
Do set times, prices, durations and dates in the mono figure style with tabular numerals.
Do mark closed or unavailable time with graphite hatching.
Do animate like ink: rules scale in from the left on scroll, stamps press (scale and slight rotation with ease-stamp), and every motion respects `prefers-reduced-motion`.
Do label placeholder frames honestly ("Portrait", numbered gallery captions) until a shop supplies photos.
donts: Don't return to the category default: a dark full-bleed interior photo, a serif shop name and a gold "Book Now".
Don't use cream, beige or warm paper; the paper is cool white.
Don't introduce a second saturated colour or hardcode a brand hex in a component.
Don't put trade imagery (scissors, combs, polish, lashes) in chrome; the template must stay trade-neutral.
Don't cast shadows from pages, rows, tabs or buttons; only the handed-over appointment card is lifted.
Don't round controls beyond the near-square scale (1.5-6px); pills are reserved for status dots.
Don't use floaty fades or rise-in-on-scroll reveals; motion is ink being laid down.
